slot.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slot.brief: Given a P-V cycle (triangle/trapezium shaped), compute net work done as area of the loop and heat absorbed per cycle using the first law over the full cycle.

stem: A gas completes the cycle $A\to C\to B\to A$ along straight-line segments on a $P$–$V$ diagram. The points are $A=(1\ \text{L},100\ \text{kPa})$, $C=(3\ \text{L},300\ \text{kPa})$ and $B=(3\ \text{L},100\ \text{kPa})$. Find the net work done by the gas and the net heat absorbed per cycle.

verdicts.working: Along AC, W = [(100 + 300)/2] × (3 − 1) = 400 J. Along CB, W = 0; along BA, W = 100 × (1 − 3) = −200 J. Thus W_net = 200 J. Over a complete cycle, ΔU = 0, so Q_net = W_net = 200 J.

working:
$W_{\rm net}=\text{area of loop}=\dfrac12(2\ \text{L})(200\ \text{kPa})=200$ J, using $1\ \text{kPa L}=1$ J.
Over a complete cycle, $\Delta U=0$; hence $Q_{\rm net}=W_{\rm net}=200$ J.

Independent check: Along AC, W = [(100 + 300)/2] × (3 − 1) = 400 J. Along CB, W = 0; along BA, W = 100 × (1 − 3) = −200 J. Thus W_net = 200 J. Over a complete cycle, ΔU = 0, so Q_net = W_net = 200 J.
